plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, daisy-like flower head made up of yellow ray florets around a dark central disk. The heads track the sun when young. It is widely grown as an ornamental and as an oil and seed crop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide, especially in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun across the sky in a behavior called heliotropism. Mature flower heads stop moving and generally face east, which helps warm them in the morning and attracts pollinators.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower of meadows, roadsides, and prairies that forms dense clonal colonies. It produces arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads that are an important late-season nectar source for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and is spread by insects. The real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up bare flower stalks in late summer, each topped with a cluster of crimson flowers with long, curved stamens. The strap-like leaves appear only after the flowers fade and last through winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early fall (August to October)
plants.location: Native to China, Korea, and Japan; widely cultivated and naturalized in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In Japan this flower blooms around the autumn equinox and is called higanbana. It is often planted around rice paddies and graveyards, partly because its toxic bulbs deter rodents.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, a bowl of pink-tipped bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and to fire in fynbos vegetation.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from late winter through early summer (August to November)
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa. The genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change his shape, in reference to the many forms of protea flowers.
